sections.h2: Who bills and collects the tax
sections.html:
City Hall houses both offices you'll deal with. Upstairs in Room 507 (200 E. Wells Street) the Assessor decides what each parcel is worth, at 414-286-3651. Down in Room 103 the City Treasurer mails the bill and takes your money, at 414-286-2240.

Milwaukee is the county seat, yet you pay the city treasurer, not a county office, since the city collects its own taxes. The bill is a combined one, and special charges or assessments can be added. Any that remain unpaid in mid-November may be rolled into the property tax bill, collected as a tax, and can't be appealed, negotiated or compromised.

An estimated 562,407 people lived in Milwaukee on July 1, 2025, a drop of 2.7 percent from April 2020. Owners occupy just 41.8 percent of housing units. Median value of an owner-occupied home: $184,000. Median gross rent: $1,059. Households: 232,520.

sections.h2: Due dates and ways to pay
sections.html:
January 31 is the deadline for the full bill or for the first installment. By default, Wis. Stat. 74.11 splits the tax into two equal halves, due January 31 and July 31, and a parcel whose total tax is below $100 must be settled in full by January 31. Milwaukee adds a longer plan, described below.

The treasurer accepts payment these ways:

  • Check by mail, in the reply envelope printed for your bill. No cash.
  • Drop box: the City Hall Market Street entrance box is available at any hour.
  • Phone (414-286-2240) or website: a card costs a 2.75 percent fee with a $3.00 floor, but a bank transfer by ACH from checking or savings costs nothing.
  • Your bank's bill-pay tool, addressed to City Treasurer, City Hall, Room 103, 200 East Wells Street, Milwaukee, WI 53202.

A letter dropped in a street mailbox may not be postmarked that day, so mail early or use a drop box. Tyler payments after 4:00 p.m. Central are credited on the next business day.

Can't cover the whole bill? The city spreads it over ten months with no interest, provided the bill is over $100 and the first payment is in by January 31. Tyler Auto Pay can pull each month's payment from a bank account or card automatically.

If you sell before the ten months are up, the treasurer can quote what remains, and the closing agent needs that number.

The next Open Book period starts the fourth Monday in April 2027. Put that date and the January 31 payment deadline on your calendar, since both repeat every year and missing either one costs money or appeal rights.

Your written objection is due at the Assessor's Office on the third Monday in May. The city prefers the Milwaukee Real Property Appeals web application at milwaukee.gov/assessorobjection, open for new forms only during Open Book. Paper is fine too, mailed to 200 E Wells Street, Room 507, Milwaukee, WI 53202, or delivered weekdays between 8:00 a.m. and 4:45 p.m. An emailed form is treated as never filed.

You can send evidence after the form. The assessor accepts these for a house:

  • An appraisal that captures the market on January 1 of this year.
  • A comparable-sales analysis from a local agent, dated the same day.
  • Pictures of repairs put off, as they stood January 1.
  • Pictures proving something listed on your property record card didn't exist on January 1.

An appraiser studies your appeal, then the Board of Assessors rules and sends notice. Still unhappy? Request a Board of Review hearing through the clerk at boardreview@milwaukee.gov or 414-286-3742. Wis. Stat. 70.47 asks for advance notice of your intent at least 48 hours before the first meeting, followed by the written objection inside that meeting's opening two hours, though the board can excuse notice for good cause. Commercial owners who skip the income and expense statement (PR-323) may be barred from testifying before the Board of Review.

Once a payment is missed, the tax is delinquent and interest accrues. Under Wis. Stat. 74.47, delinquent general property taxes and special charges bear one percent for each month or part of a month. Ordinance can add up to 0.5 percent monthly for a county board or a city authorized under s. 74.87, which is why the treasurer's payoff quote matters.

If the first installment hasn't arrived five working days past January 31, everything still owing is delinquent on February 1 (s. 74.11(7)). The interest-free city plan also hinges on that first payment.

The lottery and gaming credit is the main one for homeowners. To get it, live in the dwelling you own as your primary Wisconsin residence on January 1 of the levy year. Rental units, business property, vacant land and garages are out, and each owner gets one primary residence. Questions on city parcels go to the treasurer.

Credit absent from your bill? Apply to the treasurer by the next January 31, or make a late claim to the Department of Revenue by October 1. The credit belongs to the property, so count it when the tax is prorated between buyer and seller. Exempt owners find forms on the assessor's site, and requests are due March 1.

Find out the balance before saying yes to an offer. Bills appear in the treasurer's Resident Access system, and assessed values in the assessor's Real Property Search. Tax rates for every year since 1984 are posted too, if you want the trend.

Work through these points when you sell:

  • Request the precise balance from the treasurer, special charges from November included.
  • Check with the closing agent about how your contract divides the bill with the buyer.
  • Make sure the deed gets recorded; every permanent ownership or name change goes to the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds.
  • The buyer should file a mailing address change with the Assessor in Room 507, otherwise a refund might be mailed to you.

In a cash sale, back taxes are normally paid out of your proceeds at closing, so an unpaid balance needn't block the deal. Interest keeps accruing until payoff, so request a figure that holds through closing day.

faqs.a: January 31 for the whole bill or a first installment, with July 31 as the state default for a second. Bills over $100 can alternatively go on the city's ten-month plan with no interest, if the first payment is in by January 31.
Through the City Treasurer in City Hall Room 103 at 200 East Wells Street, by mailed check, drop box, phone or website. Cash can't be used.

faqs.q: When can I contest my value?
faqs.a: During Open Book, the fourth Monday in April through the third Monday in May. That last Monday is the yearly objection deadline, and filing goes to the Assessor's Office.
Yes. Get a payoff quote from the treasurer first, since state law charges one percent a month on late tax, and the closing agent can settle it from your proceeds if the contract permits.
The city, through its Treasurer. Deeds, and the state transfer fee, are handled by the County Register of Deeds.
